Method of Attack: The backdoor would change the behavior of the sshd binary and allow an attacker with knowledge of a specific private key to remotely execute arbitrary code on the machine.
Discoverer: Reported to the oss-security@openwall mailing list
Impacted Systems: Fedora Linux 40 beta and Fedora Rawhide
Arch Linux 2024.03.01, VM images 20240301.218094 to 20240315.221711 and container images created between and including 2024-02-24 and 2024-03-28
Attack Vector: When a malicious version of the xz-utils library is installed, a malicious shared object (SO) file is stored on disk. On Linux-based OSes, SO files are analogous to Windows DLLs. The SSH server binary sshd loads the malicious SO file from disk when it starts. This file contains the actual backdoor, which hijacks a specific OpenSSL function, RSA_public_decrypt, allowing an attacker with knowledge of a specific private SSH key to execute arbitrary code on the machine.
Indicators of Compromise: To check if a system is affected, you can run xz --version. If the output contains 5.6.0 or 5.6.1, it means you're likely running a backdoor version of xz.
